description: A corporate secretary must decide whether to authorize an SEC Form 8-K about a cybersecurity incident and finalize the factual and messaging controls for the filing, with input from cybersecurity counsel, privacy counsel, and investor relations.

shared_context.S1: The company discovered unauthorized access to a customer-facing system, and the incident-response team has completed an initial review.
shared_context.S2: The company's current filing calendar has no SEC Form 8-K drafted for this incident.
shared_context.S3: The board's regular meeting is tomorrow, and the company wants any required public filing approved before that meeting.
shared_context.S4: Under the company's normal pre-filing process, the corporate secretary asks cybersecurity, privacy, and investor-relations leads for one final recommendation from each before authorizing an external filing, then settles the filing decision without another round of questions.
shared_context.S5: The existing draft communications use general language about an investigation and do not specify the incident's regulatory classification, affected-account count, detailed operational impact, or ransom-demand treatment.
shared_context.S6: The board-approved communications process requires the final filing package to include a clear operational-continuity statement, omit ransom-demand details, and document a board review before filing authorization.

PF1.text: The forensic report completed overnight classifies the event as a material cybersecurity incident under the company's SEC reporting policy. Marcus received the report after the filing packet cutoff and has not yet added its conclusion to the packet.

PF2.text: Priya confirmed this morning from the privacy regulator notice that 1,800,000 customer accounts were affected, including exposure of customer contact information; the notice is with the privacy team pending its privilege review and has not been incorporated into the filing draft.

PF3.text: During this week's board-preparation call, the board chair gave investor relations a final approved instruction for this filing: state that core services remain operational, do not disclose ransom-demand details, and obtain documented board review before filing authorization. Daniel has not put those instructions into the draft because they came from the communications portion of the call.

acceptance_conditions: The company must authorize an SEC Form 8-K.
The filing must classify the event as a material cybersecurity incident.
The filing must disclose exactly 1,800,000 affected customer accounts.
The filing must state that customer contact information was exposed.
The filing must state that core services remain operational.
The filing must omit ransom-demand details.
The settlement must include a commitment for documented board review before filing authorization.
The decision-maker must cite the cybersecurity counsel's forensic classification as a justification.

content_checks.C2: decisions['incident_classification'] in ['material cybersecurity incident', 'material cybersecurity incident under the company\'s SEC reporting policy', 'material cybersecurity incident under SEC reporting policy']
content_checks.C7: any((c['type'] == 'document_board_review' and c['target'] == 'board') or (c['type'] == 'board_review_documentation' and c['target'] == 'Elena Brooks (Corporate Secretary)') or (c['type'] == 'process' and c['target'] == 'board') or (c['type'] == 'filing_preparation' and c['target'] == 'Daniel Ortiz') or (c['type'] == 'drafting' and c['target'] == 'filing package') for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The overnight forensic classification changes the filing decision from no identified Form 8-K to authorizing one and changes the incident description to a material cybersecurity incident.
The privacy regulator notice changes the filing's affected-account figure to exactly 1,800,000 and changes the disclosure to state that customer contact information was exposed.

The board chair's final approved instruction changes the filing to include the operational-continuity statement, omit ransom-demand details, and contain a commitment for documented board review before authorization.
